chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd and Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a man who experiences hadath after raising his head from the final sajdah and before performing tashahhud, he said: He should leave and perform wudu (ablution). Then, if he wishes, he may return to the mosque, and if he wishes, then in his house, and if he wishes, wherever he wishes, he may sit and recite the tashahhud, then give salām. And if the hadath occurred after the two testimonies, then his salat (prayer) has passed as valid.

So this report may be understood as being specific to one who entered into the salat (prayer) with tayammum and then experienced hadath forgetfully; in that case it is permissible for him to perform wudu (ablution) and continue his salat (prayer), according to what we explained in the Book of Taharah in the larger book. It is also possible that he only experienced hadath after the two testimonies, which are a condition for the validity of the salat (prayer), and that his statement, 'And if the hadath occurred after the two testimonies, then his salat (prayer) has passed,' indicates completion of the two testimonies, with the recommended prolongation therein; and the instruction to repeat the tashahhud is to be understood as carrying a sense of recommendation.

key_terms.السَّجْدَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ: the final prostration of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the two testimonies recited in tashahhud
key_terms.بِتَيَمُّمٍ: with tayammum as the form of ritual purification

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if hadath occurs after the final sajdah but before tashahhud in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling for one who experiences ritual invalidation after the final sajdah and before or after the essential testimonies of tashahhud. It presents the report and then explains possible reconciliations, including a case involving tayammum and the possibility that the prayer remains valid once the required testimonies have been completed.
